question.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+y-3z=7 \\ kx-4y+z=-19 \\ x-y-4z=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that  $z=-2$ and that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $7k+23,$ find the value of $k.$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's write the determinant of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -3 \\ k & -4 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}|=7k+23\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $z$ is given by $z=\frac{{D}_{z}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{z}=|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 7 \\ k & -4 & -19 \\ 1 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & -19 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}k & -19 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}|+7\cdot |\begin{aligned}k & -4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-16-19)-(4k+19)+7(-k+4) \\  & =-70-4k-19-7k+28 \\  & =-61-11k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
z=\frac{{D}_{z}}{D}=\frac{-61-11k}{7k+23}.
$$

From the problem statement, we know that $z=-2.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-61-11k}{7k+23} & =-2 \\ -61-11k & =-14k-46 \\ 3k & =15 \\ k & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
